query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn system was selected to reduce cost while retaining the mechanical performance of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi; prior work reported comparable or better mechanical properties after excluding Co. Research on FeNiCrMn has mainly addressed corrosion, while studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys examined dynamic responses under tension or compression, different temperatures and strain rates, compositional changes, and the presence of cracks or voids. Those studies established that dynamic properties are sensitive to loading regime and material condition, but their different chemistries and defect states do not identify what governs FeNiCrMn. Under the constraints of retaining the Co-free composition and its strength–ductility balance, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains the dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes? Define a controlled study capable of testing the hypothesis, its applicable boundaries, the prior findings that support it, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The dominant mechanism controlling the dynamic strength and ductility of solidified equiatomic FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain‐rate regimes is the temperature‐ and rate‐dependent activation of deformation twinning, enabled by its medium stacking fault energy. At low temperatures (<0 °C) and high strain rates (>10^3 s^−1), deformation twinning contributes a significant twin boundary density that elevates work‐hardening and ductility; at high temperatures (>400 °C) or low strain rates (<10^−3 s^−1), plasticity proceeds primarily by dislocation slip with minimal twinning, yielding lower hardening and ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: Single‐phase fcc equiatomic Fe25Ni25Cr25Mn25 alloy produced by arc melting, homogenized at 1100 °C for 24 h, rolled to 2 mm thickness, average grain size ~20 µm, free of pre‐existing twins or precipitates.
generation.intervention: A full factorial mechanical test matrix: uniaxial compression and tension tests at temperatures −196 °C, 0 °C, 25 °C, 200 °C, 400 °C, 600 °C and strain rates 10^−3 s^−1, 10^−1 s^−1, 10^1 s^−1, 10^3 s^−1, 10^4 s^−1.
generation.conditions: Inert‐gas environment to prevent oxidation, thermally stabilized specimens (±1 °C), L/D=3 for compression, dog‐bone geometry for tension, strain measured by high‐speed extensometry for high‐rate tests.
generation.structural_mediator: Volume fraction of deformation twins and twin‐boundary density measured post‐test by EBSD and TEM.
generation.mechanism: At low T and high rates the medium stacking fault energy (~20 mJ m^−2) promotes deformation twinning, which introduces twin boundaries that act as barriers to dislocation motion, elevating work‐hardening and maintaining ductility. At high T or low rates, increased cross‐slip and climb favor dislocation slip over twinning, reducing hardening and ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the quasi‐static baseline at 25 °C/10^−3 s^−1, yield strength and work‐hardening rate increase by ~20–30% and twin volume fraction rises above ~15% under conditions ≤0 °C and ≥10^3 s^−1. Under ≥400 °C or ≤10^−3 s^−1, twin fraction falls below ~5%, with strength and ductility comparable to or lower than baseline.
generation.baseline: Quasi‐static compression at 25 °C, 10^−3 s^−1: yield strength ~400 MPa, total elongation ~50%, twin fraction ~5%.
generation.boundary: Valid for single‐phase fcc equiatomic FeNiCrMn with grain size 10–50 µm, T range −196 °C to 600 °C, strain rates 10^−3 s^−1 to 10^4 s^−1, no second‐phase particles.
generation.uncertainty: Exact twin activation thresholds and quantitative twin fractions are approximate; potential contributions of dynamic strain aging or solute drag are not excluded.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct the full factorial temperature/strain‐rate matrix on homogenized FeNiCrMn specimens, then characterize post‐deformation twin volume fraction and dislocation structure by EBSD and TEM.
measurements: Stress‐strain curves (yield strength, work‐hardening rate, ductility)
Dislocation density and slip trace analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If deformation twin fractions remain below ~5% across all temperature/strain‐rate conditions or if variations in strength and ductility do not correlate with twin fractions (i.e. enhanced strength/ductility without increased twinning), then the hypothesis is falsified.
